findings.title: procs_lock is initialized but never used
findings.body: The new `pthread_mutex_t procs_lock` is declared in `ta.h` with the comment *"protects vm->procs[] access"*, initialized in `vm_new`, and destroyed in `vm_free` — but no code anywhere calls `pthread_mutex_lock`/`unlock` on it (confirmed via grep). This is either dead code that should be removed, or an incomplete fix: `vm->procs[]` is accessed concurrently without synchronization in several places — e.g. `io_poller_thread` iterates all slots (line 357-380) while a worker thread's `vm_spawn` → `proc_new` writes new entries (line 221) and other workers read slots via `vm->procs[pid]` (line 453). If the intent was to guard `procs[]`, the guard is missing and TSAN races on the table remain unresolved.

overall_explanation: The atomic type conversions (`vm->stop`, `vm->yield_requested`, `vm->main_dead`, `p->state`) are functionally correct — C11 makes plain assignment/read of `_Atomic`-qualified variables atomic automatically, so even unconverted access sites like `vm->stop = 1` or `p->state == PROC_RUNNING` are now atomic operations. The one actionable issue is the `procs_lock` mutex that is initialized and destroyed but never locked anywhere, despite its documented purpose of protecting `vm->procs[]`.
